correctness.rationale: PASS: In the Fock normalization, a disk of radius sqrt(R) has top localization eigenvalue ell=1-e^{-R}, second ell_1=1-(1+R)e^{-R} and gap R e^{-R}. Coherent centers separated by d give overlap magnitude e^{-d^2/2}; compact translation decoupling bounds residual sector by ell_1+o(1). Alien-disk coherent mass is <=R exp(-(d-sqrt R)^2); positivity gives square-root block coupling and Schur complement yields O_R(exp(-(d-sqrt R)^2)) error. The three-state Gram phases have cyclic product exp(i sqrt(3)d^2/2), eigenvalues 1+2s cos((Phi+2pi q)/3). Rotation decomposes the original operator into three fixed character sectors, giving genuine double crossings by continuity near integer and half-integer flux, while the fourth eigenvalue stays separated. Quantifiers fix R>0 and take d->infinity. This is an analytic argument; direct numerical quadrature of the complete Toeplitz operator was not independently repeated.
residual_risks: Fixed R>0, large d, equilateral equal disks only.
Only existence, not uniqueness, of each degeneracy near a flux lattice point.
